metadata.description: A non-human identity/account — an ACTOR (automation, an agent, a provider integration, an API-key holder) that the control plane authenticates and authorizes (the RBAC bridge — `Grouping` subject_bindings plus the function-capability matrix). actor_type `service_account`. Holds no secret material — credentials referenced (CredentialRef). Backs the built-in provider's static_api_key/service accounts.

handle.description: Login handle / username, unique within the implementation.

display_name.description: Converted verbatim from the flat Identity.Person spec.

authenticated_by.description: handle/uuid of the Auth Provider (auth capability) or DirectoryService that authenticates this person. Default: the built-in provider (no external IdP required).

credential_ref.description: Reference to CredentialRef — the credential record for this person. Common-elements Reference shape (handle string or {uuid, handle} object); resolvable and policy-walkable, never an opaque string.

status.description: Converted verbatim from the flat Identity.Person spec.

owner_ref.description: Reference to Identity.Person or IdentityGroup — the owning identity accountable for this account. Common-elements Reference shape (handle string or {uuid, handle} object); resolvable and policy-walkable, never an opaque string.

actor_uuid.description: The stable actor id referenced by role-assignments and grouping (access_grouping) membership.

relationships.description: Member of an access grouping / IdentityGroup; membership drives role binding.

adopts.role: identity/subject vocabulary (userName, displayName, active, userType; a person and a service account are both Users)

context.purpose: Models a non-human account — automation, an agent, a provider integration — as an authenticated, auditable actor.
context.plain_description: An account for something that is not a person: a pipeline, an agent, an integration holding an API key. Like a person it has a required `handle` and `actor_type` (always `service_account`), an authenticator, and referenced-only credentials; unlike a person it declares an `owner_ref` — the person or group accountable for it. Its stable actor id is what role assignments and audit records bind to.
use_when: You need automation to authenticate with its own identity instead of borrowing a person's.
You need every non-human credential holder to have a named accountable owner.
not_for: The API key or token itself — CredentialRef, referenced not stored.
works_with: CredentialRef — the account's key/token, by reference.
IdentityGroup — memberships that grant it roles.
